checks.why: a module-level exported const has the modules that import it as dependents, instead of nothing at all
and --delete does not call it safe
an imported const read through a member access or passed as an argument is resolved to the declaration the import binds, not matched by name
the same for a const that holds a call's result, handed to a call
a const read in a type (`typeof X`): in a parameter's type it is the function's read, in a type alias the module's, each at its own line
control: a file that imports the same name from ANOTHER declaration is not a reader of this one
